narrativeReportMd:
# Invoice R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Invoice` remains the same resource, but R6 has local breaking changes. The strongest R4→R6 issues are `Invoice.date` being renamed to `Invoice.creation`, removal of the required price-component code `deduction`, and replacing Invoice-local price component backbone content with `MonetaryComponent`.

## Scope
The report covers local Invoice element, binding, reference-target, serialization/codegen, and R6-to-R4 representability changes. Inherited base-artifact changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
Migration needs version-aware field renames, price component terminology review, regenerated models/profiles for `MonetaryComponent`, and explicit R6→R4 rules for new period fields and widened references.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `date`→`creation`, `deduction` removal, `MonetaryComponent` adoption, and `lineItem.chargeItem[x]` losing its computable ChargeItem-only target.

## Findings requiring human review
Review the price-component terminology consolidation and the unconstrained R6 chargeItem Reference, because business semantics and ballot intent are not fully established by the computable files alone.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive by retaining old aliases/codes or listing added reference targets explicitly, but R6 appears to normalize monetary modeling and broaden some actor/reference domains.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Invoice` has material local breaking changes. Top concerns: `date`→`creation`, `deduction` disappearing from required price-component terminology, and price components moving to `MonetaryComponent`; the largest uncertainty is whether the unconstrained R6 `lineItem.chargeItem[x]` Reference is intentional.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Use explicit R4/R6 transforms. Rename posting date fields, map price-component terminology with business review, regenerate code for `MonetaryComponent`, and decide how R6-only `period[x]`, `serviced[x]`, Practitioner issuers, and non-ChargeItem references are handled on R4 export.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: High confidence for structural deltas because they come from primary local StructureDefinitions and complete CodeSystems. Medium confidence for rationale and prevalence because official diffs, narrative change notes, profiles, and instance corpus were unavailable.

findings.title: Invoice.date was renamed to Invoice.creation

semanticText.definition: Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.
Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.

newState.narrativeMd: `Invoice.creation` has the same type/cardinality/definition; `Invoice.date` is absent.

facts.oldValue: Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.
facts.newValue: Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same type, cardinality, summary flag, and definition identify `creation` as the successor to `date`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `date` uses an element not declared in R6; R6 `creation` likewise needs mapping for R4. Generated properties, FHIRPath, serializers, and profiles must change.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Posting dates affect billing timing, payment terms, audit, and reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Distinguish invoice creation/posting from service/billing period.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Invoice.date` as the posting/creation date, clarify its short text, and add `period[x]` for billing/service periods.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears to be clearer separation between invoice posting/creation time and the new billing/service period. That goal is reasonable, but the supplied definitions show `date` and `creation` have the same cardinality, type, summary flag, and definition. Because the goal could largely be met by retaining `date` with clearer wording while adding `period[x]`, the breaking rename looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would keep `Invoice.date` as the posting date, perhaps with an alias/deprecation note or improved short description, and rely on the newly added `Invoice.period[x]` to represent the billed service period. This avoids invalidating R4 instances and avoids duplicate same-resource fields; the tradeoff is that implementers must tolerate the older, broader name rather than the cleaner `creation` name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire compatibility at the cost of living with the less precise R4 element name.

evidence.quote: Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.
Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.

findings.narrativeMd: `Invoice.date` changed wire/property identity. Existing R4 data with `date` must be transformed before strict R6 validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs when `date` is present. R6 `creation` is R4-representable only through an explicit rename back to `date`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `date` to `creation` in transforms, generated models, FHIRPath, mappings, profiles, and tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias would have preserved old data but added model redundancy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Invoice.date` and R6 `Invoice.creation` have the same cardinality, type, summary flag, and definition, while the old wire name disappears. An R4 invoice carrying a posting date will fail strict R6 structural validation unless transformed, and generated models, FHIRPath, mappings, and profile paths that use `date` must be changed. Even though Invoice is low maturity, this path is central to invoice timing and audit/business workflows, so the rename looks more disruptive than the model goal requires.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `Invoice.date`: `0..1 dateTime`, summary, definition `Date/time(s) of when this Invoice was posted.`
R6 StructureDefinition has no `Invoice.date`; `Invoice.creation` is `0..1 dateTime`, summary, with the same posting-date definition.
HL7 R4 Invoice scope describes invoices as billing documents and says tracking financial information is vital in patient administration and finance systems: https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/invoice.html
Quick web check found public R4 Invoice profiling in the ABDM/NRCeS IG, but no prevalence corpus.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Invoice is FMM 0 and trial-use, which softens the stability concern and prevents assuming broad production blast radius. The low maturity does not fully excuse this rename because posting date is a central billing/audit field and public IG evidence shows implementation relevance.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `date` contain an element not present in the R6 Invoice StructureDefinition; runtime/API/codegen also changes because the generated property name becomes `creation`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could have kept `Invoice.date` as the posting/creation date, clarified its short text, and added `period[x]` for service/billing periods. That preserves old instances without duplicate date fields; the tradeoff is retaining a less precise legacy name.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard rename and a plausible lower-cost alternative. I add more low-FMM caution, but the central billing/audit role still supports `Revisit`.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize price component terminology for shared MonetaryComponent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `deduction` as a deprecated transitional code in the shared `price-component-type` code system.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing price component terminology for shared `MonetaryComponent` is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R6 `discount` definition explicitly says it may be referred to as a deduction. A base-design alternative exists, but it is only partial because retaining `deduction` would perpetuate ambiguous discount/deduction coding in a required shared value set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would include `deduction` in `price-component-type` as deprecated or legacy while making `discount` the preferred code. That would preserve R4-valid instances. The material tradeoff is indefinite duplicate representation for reductions: validators and downstream accounting logic would need to accept both codes, and deprecated terminology can persist for many release cycles. A ConceptMap alone would be useful migration guidance but is not a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 `deduction` instances but keeps two overlapping reduction codes in a required shared terminology.

evidence.quote: the amount is a deduction applied on the base price.
This is sometimes referred to as a deduction.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 `deduction` price components are no longer valid against the R6 required binding. This is both a validation break and a financial semantics risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances with `deduction` can fail R6 validation. R6 uses only codes R4 also allowed, so reverse code membership is low risk.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `deduction` uses, define a reviewed mapping to `discount` or an extension, and update generated enums/tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated retained code or ConceptMap would have reduced disruption while still guiding convergence.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required price-component type binding no longer accepts the R4 `deduction` code. R6 appears to fold that concept into `discount`, but R4 had both `deduction` and `discount`, so migration may require accounting or contract-specific judgment rather than a purely mechanical code rewrite. Because this is a required-bound financial classification used to explain invoice totals, the break deserves renewed review despite the resource's low maturity.
keyEvidence: R4 `Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent.type` is `1..1 code` with required binding to `invoice-priceComponentType|4.0.1`.
R4 CodeSystem `invoice-priceComponentType` includes `deduction` and separately includes `discount`.

R6 `MonetaryComponent.type` is `1..1 code` with required binding to `price-component-type|6.0.0-ballot4`; the R6 CodeSystem has no `deduction` code and defines `discount` as sometimes referred to as a deduction.
HL7 R4 Invoice scope and the ABDM/NRCeS R4 Invoice profile show billing implementation relevance; no quick corpus evidence for deduction frequency was found.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the burden to preserve every code, especially in a newly evolving financial resource. However, required-bound billing terminology directly affects validation, generated enums, and financial interpretation, so low FMM only softens rather than removes the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 price component with `type` = `deduction` is outside the R6 required value set; runtime/API/codegen also changes because generated enum members and switch logic lose that code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `deduction` in the shared `price-component-type` CodeSystem as deprecated or legacy while making `discount` preferred. That would preserve R4-valid instances and allow gradual convergence, with the real tradeoff of maintaining overlapping reduction codes in a required shared terminology.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly calls out a hard required-binding break and a partial alternative. I judge the alternative more important than the prior `probably justified` framing because the mapping can be financially semantic, not just lexical.

findings.title: Invoice price components now use the shared MonetaryComponent datatype

oldState.summary: R4 lineItem.priceComponent is an Invoice-owned BackboneElement; totalPriceComponent contentReferences it.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 local child paths include `.type`, `.code`, `.factor`, `.amount`; BackboneElement also allows `modifierExtension`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps similar child names via a shared datatype, but generated type/path ownership changes and `MonetaryComponent` has no `modifierExtension`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 assigns the same price component elements to `MonetaryComponent`, which has matching main children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Common child JSON mostly survives, but generated classes, profile paths, and R4 priceComponent `modifierExtension` content break.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Financial qualifier extensions can affect interpretation of totals.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse a shared monetary component datatype.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the Invoice-local priceComponent backbone in R6 while aligning its semantics and binding with `MonetaryComponent`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Reusing a common `MonetaryComponent` datatype is a reasonable architectural goal. A less-breaking path could preserve many R4 instances and generated paths, but it would leave Invoice with a local financial-component model instead of fully adopting the shared type, so the alternative has material long-term modeling and tooling costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent` and `Invoice.totalPriceComponent` as the old Invoice-owned backbone for one release, update its definitions and required binding to align with `MonetaryComponent`, and publish mapping to the shared datatype. This would preserve R4 local paths and `modifierExtension` on the backbone. The cost is duplicate definitions for the same monetary fact, profile divergence, less reuse across resources, and the risk that the legacy representation never disappears.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old paths and modifierExtension-bearing instances but delays or weakens shared datatype standardization.

evidence.quote: Extensions that cannot be ignored even if unrecognized

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces Invoice-local price component backbone content with `MonetaryComponent`. This normalizes modeling but breaks generated nested classes, local profile paths, and modifierExtension-bearing R4 price components.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 price components with only common children and allowed codes often transform cleanly. R4 `modifierExtension` on priceComponent is old-valid/new-invalid because R6 MonetaryComponent does not allow it.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models, update profile/FHIRPath references to `MonetaryComponent`, and audit priceComponent modifierExtension use before migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Publishing explicit mappings and extension guidance would reduce disruption while preserving R6 normalization.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This is a local Invoice type replacement finding, not a duplicate base DataType/BackboneElement report.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 changes `lineItem.priceComponent` and `totalPriceComponent` from Invoice-owned backbone content to the shared `MonetaryComponent` datatype. This is a real generated-model and profiling change, and R4 modifier extensions on the local backbone no longer have the same valid home. But ordinary price component children such as `type`, `code`, `factor`, and `amount` retain a very similar wire shape, and adopting a shared monetary datatype is a coherent base-model goal.
keyEvidence: R4 `Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent` is a `BackboneElement`; `Invoice.totalPriceComponent` content-references `#Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent`.
R4 snapshot includes `Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent.modifierExtension` as `0..* Extension`.
R6 `Invoice.lineItem.priceComponent` and `Invoice.totalPriceComponent` both have type `MonetaryComponent`.
R6 `MonetaryComponent` has `type`, `code`, `factor`, and `amount`, and its snapshot has no `modifierExtension` element.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern substantially. In a low-maturity resource, normalizing a repeated financial modeling pattern into a shared datatype can justify codegen and profile migration, especially when common instance children largely carry forward.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated nested classes and profile paths move from an Invoice-owned backbone to `MonetaryComponent`; old-valid/new-invalid occurs for R4 price components that actually use `modifierExtension`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep the Invoice-local backbone for one transition release while aligning its children and terminology with `MonetaryComponent`. That preserves old profile paths and modifierExtension-bearing instances, but it delays the shared datatype goal and creates duplicate definitions for the same monetary concept.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies codegen/profile disruption and modifierExtension loss, and the partial alternative is fair. I would not treat the whole change as uniformly high-impact because common price-component JSON without modifier extensions mostly remains structurally recognizable.

findings.title: Invoice.issuer can now reference Practitioner and PractitionerRole as well as Organization

newState.summary: R6 issuer allows Organization, Practitioner, or PractitionerRole.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old Organization issuers remain valid; R6 Practitioner/PractitionerRole issuers are not directly R4-representable.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The target widening preserves R4 `Organization` issuers; no R4-to-R6 compatibility alternative is needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Changing the short label from issuing organization to issuing entity and allowing Practitioner/PractitionerRole is a reasonable expressiveness improvement. Since every R4-valid `Organization` issuer remains valid in R6, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using an extension for individual or role issuers would be an R4 backport/down-conversion strategy, not a less-breaking base R6 alternative. The base R6 design can widen the target list without invalidating R4 instances; the tradeoff belongs to R6-to-R4 export and to consumers that assumed only Organization.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 export needs policy for Practitioner and PractitionerRole issuers, but R4 instances remain valid in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: The issuer target domain widened. This is forward-compatible but can break R4 exports and code that casts issuer to Organization.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 is safe for Organization issuers; R6→R4 needs mapping, extension, or rejection for Practitioner/PractitionerRole.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Handle all R6 issuer target types and define R4 export policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Explicit extension/alternate element would have preserved R4 type expectations but reduced base expressiveness.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The issuer reference target list widens from Organization-only to Organization, Practitioner, and PractitionerRole. Existing R4 Organization issuers remain valid R6 content. R6-to-R4 export and consumers that hard-cast issuer to Organization need policy updates, but the base R6 change is an additive expressiveness improvement rather than an R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: R4 `Invoice.issuer` is `0..1 Reference(Organization)`.
R6 `Invoice.issuer` is `0..1 Reference(Organization | Practitioner | PractitionerRole)`.
The element remains optional and non-modifier in both versions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further reduces concern for this additive widening. Low maturity is not needed to justify the change, because R4-valid issuer references are preserved.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 Practitioner or PractitionerRole issuers have no direct R4 base target, but R4 Organization issuers remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for forward compatibility. Keeping Organization-only would avoid some reverse-conversion policy, but it would block the stated expressiveness gain; an extension would be a down-conversion/backport strategy, not a better R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly notes R6-to-R4 and type-assumption risk. I disagree with treating this as a material problem under the fresh path-level rubric because the target change is widening and preserves R4 instances.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Reference branch is constrained to ChargeItem.

facts.note: No targetProfile means unconstrained Reference in the base StructureDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Element unchanged except target profile; intended semantics uncertain because narrative still names ChargeItem.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old ChargeItem references remain valid, but R6 can structurally allow references R4 rejects and billing logic may not know how to process.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Line item charge references drive pricing, audit, and adjudication details.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly broaden references or defer to profiles; unclear.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R4 ChargeItem references remain valid; the concern is R6 validation clarity and R6-to-R4 representability, not R4-to-R6 compatibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 computable targetProfile is absent while the narrative still describes a ChargeItem. Because the supplied evidence does not identify intended non-ChargeItem targets, the unconstrained Reference is not clearly justified even though it does not invalidate R4 ChargeItem references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For base R6 design clarity, the specification could have retained `Reference(ChargeItem)` or explicitly listed any additional intended targets. That would improve validation and interoperability, but it is not counted as a backward-compatible alternative here because R4-to-R6 preservation is already satisfied; the remaining issue is an R6-to-R4 and runtime interoperability risk.

evidence.detail: R6 text still says ChargeItem contains details.
evidence.quote: The ChargeItem contains information such as the billing code, date, amount etc.

findings.narrativeMd: A required line item reference branch lost its ChargeItem-only target profile. This can surprise validators and runtime code that dereference and cast to ChargeItem.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4→R6 break for ChargeItem references. R6 instances with other targets are not cleanly R4-representable and may break consumers.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not assume R6 chargeItemReference is ChargeItem unless a profile states it. For R4 export, map, reject, or convert to CodeableConcept where safe.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less disruptive option was to retain ChargeItem and add explicit extra targets if needed.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm whether missing targetProfile is intentional.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes the computable `ChargeItem` target profile from the required `chargeItem[x]` Reference branch while leaving the narrative text about a ChargeItem unchanged. This does not invalidate R4 ChargeItem references, but it makes base R6 structurally permit references that R4 cannot represent and that billing logic may not know how to process. Because the line-item charge reference is central to invoice pricing and audit, the loss of computable target clarity deserves standards review rather than being dismissed as mere widening.
keyEvidence: R4 `Invoice.lineItem.chargeItem[x]` is `1..1` with `Reference(ChargeItem)` or `CodeableConcept`.
R6 `Invoice.lineItem.chargeItem[x]` is `1..1` with `Reference` or `CodeableConcept`; the Reference type has no targetProfile in the differential or snapshot.
R4 and R6 definitions both say the `ChargeItem` contains billing code, date, amount, and related details.
HL7 R4 Invoice scope describes line items as collected ChargeItems used to calculate invoice prices.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens general stability expectations, but this path is directly tied to the core billing line-item model. The low maturity does not eliminate concern because the change affects validation clarity, downstream dereferencing, and R6-to-R4 representability for central invoice content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can now structurally carry non-ChargeItem references that R4 rejects; runtime/API/codegen risk arises when validators and billing code can no longer rely on a computable ChargeItem target.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `Reference(ChargeItem)` or explicitly listed any additional intended targets. That would preserve R4 behavior and validation clarity; the tradeoff is reduced flexibility if R6 intentionally wanted arbitrary reference targets, but that goal is not evident from the unchanged narrative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly flags high runtime and R6-to-R4 risk and uncertainty. I disagree with `Not applicable` for alternatives because retaining or explicitly enumerating target profiles is a direct less-risk base design choice.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the change is already additive. An R4 extension bridge can help down-conversion, but that is migration/backport guidance rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a root billing period. This is useful but creates R6-only information for down-conversion.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `Invoice.period[x]` for the billing or service period. This is a forward-compatible addition: R4 invoices do not become invalid, and R6 gains a native place for information that R4 lacked. Down-conversion can lose information or require an extension, but that is not a reason to revisit the additive R6 base design.
keyEvidence: R4 Invoice snapshot has no `Invoice.period[x]` element.
R6 `Invoice.period[x]` is optional `0..1` with choices `date` and `Period`, summary, definition `Date/time(s) range of services included in this invoice.`
R6 also keeps a separate posting timestamp as `Invoice.creation`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use reinforces the low concern. The change is optional and additive, so the low maturity mainly confirms that reverse-conversion limitations should not be treated as a design break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `periodDate` or `periodPeriod` has no direct R4 base element, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed because the element is additive. An R4 extension or cross-version mapping can help export, but that is migration support rather than a less-breaking R6 design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies reverse-conversion risk and the lack of a needed base alternative. I disagree with framing it as medium impact for fresh R4-to-R6 review because it is optional additive content.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow line-level timing without dereferencing ChargeItem.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional `Invoice.lineItem.serviced[x]` is additive and does not invalidate R4 line items.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing a line item to carry service timing directly is a reasonable R6 goal, especially when an inline `CodeableConcept` charge item is used. The optional addition preserves R4-to-R6 compatibility; the compatibility issue is only lossless R6-to-R4 representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping timing only on referenced `ChargeItem` or using an R4 extension are down-conversion or profiling strategies, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives. Since the element is optional, R4 instances remain valid while R6 gains a native place for line-level timing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Supports self-contained R6 line timing while requiring R4 export policy for R6-only timing data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional line-level service timing with `Invoice.lineItem.serviced[x]`. R4 line items remain valid in R6, and the new field supplies a native location for timing that previously had to live in a referenced ChargeItem, an extension, or local context. R6-to-R4 export needs policy, but the base addition itself is compatibility-preserving.
keyEvidence: R4 `Invoice.lineItem` has no `serviced[x]` child.
R6 `Invoice.lineItem.serviced[x]` is optional `0..1` with choices `date` and `Period`.
R6 definition says the field captures when the service was delivered or completed.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers stability pressure and supports accepting this optional model growth. Since no R4 instance is invalidated, low maturity is more than sufficient to avoid a revisit judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 service timing at line level has no direct R4 base slot, but there is no R4-to-R6 instance or generated-property removal.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed. Forcing timing to stay only on referenced ChargeItem would preserve R4 shape but would also prevent the R6 model from representing timing for inline CodeableConcept line items; R4 extensions are migration aids, not a better R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly notes R6-to-R4 export work and no base alternative. I disagree with treating this optional addition as a meaningful breaking concern under the fresh review rubric.
